summary:
**Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer**

**What we developed**
The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive web-based simulator that lets learners train like a real astronaut. It offers a 7-phase program, from Physical Conditioning and Spacecraft Systems to Spacewalk Training, Emergency Procedures and Final Certification. A solar system explorer adds planet cards with missions for each world, while XP, ranks and badges track progress. Orbit, an AI robot guide, supports learners at every step. The project is built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with space-themed visuals and audio.
The NASA Space Apps challenge was to make complex space science engaging and accessible to young learners. The main difficulties were balancing scientific accuracy with fun, designing a clear progression where phases unlock in order, and keeping the interface simple yet immersive.
Space careers depend on STEM skills, yet many students find these subjects abstract. By turning learning into missions and rewards, the trainer builds curiosity, retention and confidence. It shows how technology can bring space education to anyone with a browser, inspiring the next generation of explorers.
details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: Project Details

Overview

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive web app for the NASA Space Apps challenge. It lets a learner go through astronaut training step by step, from physical conditioning to a final certification. It combines a structured training program, a solar system explorer, game-style rewards and an AI guide named Orbit.

Objective

The aim is to make space science and astronaut training engaging and easy to follow. Learners earn progress by completing missions and quizzes instead of only reading facts.

Key Features

  • Home page ("Mission Control"): a hero section with live stats for phases done, missions and XP, plus two entry points: Start Training and Explore Planets.
  • 7-phase training program: the phases unlock in order, and each shows its XP reward and time.
  • Solar system explorer: one card per planet with its type, moons and diameter, and 3 missions per planet with a progress tracker.
  • Gamification: XP, ranks (starting at Cadet), badges and a progress bar.
  • Orbit, the AI robot guide: a chat companion that welcomes the learner and helps through every phase.
  • Ambient audio toggle: optional background sound for immersion.

The 7 Training Phases

  1. Physical Conditioning (100 XP): preparing the body for high G-forces and zero gravity.
  2. Spacecraft Systems (150 XP): life support, propulsion, navigation, communications and power.
  3. Orbital Mechanics (200 XP): orbital velocity, transfer orbits and rendezvous.
  4. Spacewalk Training (250 XP): extravehicular activity, safety tethers and movement in zero gravity.
  5. Emergency Procedures (300 XP): fire, depressurization, medical emergencies and system failures.
  6. Mission Planning (350 XP): trajectories, resources and scientific objectives.
  7. Final Certification (500 XP): a full mission simulation that combines everything learned.

Playable Simulation

I also built a single-file HTML game, junior_astronaut_simulator.html, that runs a full mission in four stages: launch to orbit, in-orbit failure and repair, station docking, and a Mars landing. It has an HD space background, shooting stars and sound effects. A pygame version, junior_astronaut_trainer.py, covers a quiz, docking and an asteroid-field game.

Technology

The project uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with canvas graphics for the simulation. Python with pygame was used for the desktop version.

Challenges

  • Keeping the science accurate while keeping it fun.
  • Designing a fair unlock system so progress feels earned.
  • Balancing game difficulty, for example speed limits when docking and landing.
  • Giving the interface a consistent space theme.

Impact and Future Scope

The trainer makes STEM topics feel like missions rather than lessons, which builds curiosity and retention. Future work could add interactive simulations inside every phase, a certificate download, more planet quizzes, multiple languages and a progress leaderboard.
